arxiv-2011-04805.title: Instantaneous time mirrors and wave equations with time-singular coefficients
arxiv-2011-04805.creator: Olivier Pinaud
arxiv-2011-04805.description: Abstract We study in this work the concept of instantaneous time mirrors that were recently introduced in the physics literature in [ 1 ] . Instantaneous time mirrors offer a new method for time reversal with a simplified experimental setup compared to classical techniques.

arxiv-2102-12111.title: Deep Learning Approach for Singer Voice Classification of Vietnamese Popular Music Conference: The Tenth International Symposium on Information and Communication Technology; December 4–6, 2019; Hanoi - Ha Long Bay, Vietnam, Viet Nam The Tenth International Symposium on Information and Communication
arxiv-2102-12111.creator: Toan Pham Van, Ngoc Tran Ngo Quang, Ta Minh Thanh
arxiv-2102-12111.description: Abstract . Singer voice classification is a meaningful task in the digital era. With a huge number of songs today, identifying a singer is very helpful for music information retrieval, music properties indexing, and so on. In this paper, we propose a new method to identify the singer’s name based on analysis of Vietnamese popular music.

arxiv-2102-13619.title: One-Dimensional Fuzzy Dark Matter Models: Structure Growth and Asymptotic Dynamics
arxiv-2102-13619.creator: Tim Zimmermann, Nico Schwersenz, Massimo Pietroni, Sandro Wimberger
arxiv-2102-13619.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Tim Zimmermann, Nico Schwersenz, Massimo Pietroni, Sandro Wimberger. This paper investigates the feasibility of simulating Fuzzy Dark Matter (FDM) with a reduced number of spatial dimensions. Our aim is to set up a realistic, yet numerically inexpensive, toy model in ( 1 + 1 ) (1+1) -dimensional space time, that — under well controlled system conditions — is capable of realizing important aspects of the full-fledged ( 3 + 1 ) (3+1) -FDM phenomenology by means of one-dimensional analogues.

arxiv-2104-00846.title: A Sieve Stochastic Gradient Descent Estimator for Online Nonparametric Regression in Sobolev ellipsoids
arxiv-2104-00846.creator: Tianyu Zhang, Noah Simon
arxiv-2104-00846.description: Abstract The goal of regression is to recover an unknown underlying function that best links a set of predictors to an outcome from noisy observations. In nonparametric regression, one assumes that the regression function belongs to a pre-specified infinite-dimensional function space (the hypothesis space).

arxiv-2105-10327.title: Weighted Burrows-Wheeler Compression
arxiv-2105-10327.creator: Aharon Fruchtman, Yoav Gross, Shmuel T. Klein, Dana Shapira
arxiv-2105-10327.description: Abstract A weight based dynamic compression method has recently been proposed, which is especially suitable for the encoding of files with locally skewed distributions. Its main idea is to assign larger weights to closer to be encoded symbols by means of an increasing weight function, rather than considering each position in the text evenly.

arxiv-2106-10966.title: Consequence Relations
arxiv-2106-10966.creator: A. Citkin, A. Muravitsky
arxiv-2106-10966.description: Abstract From one perspective, all intellectual and artistic pursuits are efforts to understand the world, including ourselves and our relation to the rest of the world. If successful, they would not ‘leave everything as it is’ but bring about some, however slight, desired change of the world in the form of modifications of our surroundings or our consciousness.

arxiv-2203-04543.title: Smeared Mass Source Wormholes in Modified f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) Gravity with the Lorentzian Density Distribution Function
arxiv-2203-04543.creator: and S. Upadhyay
arxiv-2203-04543.description: Abstract Wormholes are speculative structures linking disparate space-time points. Their geometry can be obtained by solving Einstein equations with tolerating the violation of null energy conditions. Recently, many researchers have studied different wormholes according to different criteria, and they achieved remarkable results.

arxiv-2208-14268.title: Optimal Power Allocation for Integrated Visible Light Positioning and Communication System with a Single LED-Lamp
arxiv-2208-14268.creator: Shuai Ma, Ruixin Yang, Bing Li, Yongyan Chen, Hang Li, Youlong Wu, Majid Safari, Shiyin Li, Naofal Al-Dhahir
arxiv-2208-14268.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate an integrated visible light positioning and communication (VLPC) system with a single LED-lamp. First, by leveraging the fact that the VLC channel model is a function of the receiver’s location, we propose a system model that estimates the channel state information (CSI) based on the positioning information without transmitting pilot sequences.

arxiv-2210-13943.title: D D - and A A -Optimal Screening Designs
arxiv-2210-13943.creator: Jonathan Stallrich
arxiv-2210-13943.description: Abstract In practice, optimal screening designs for arbitrary run sizes are traditionally generated using the D D -criterion with factor settings fixed at ± 1 \pm 1 , even when considering continuous factors with levels in [ − 1 , 1 ] [-1,1] .

arxiv-2309-13801.title: A Formalized Extension of the Substitution Lemma in Coq
arxiv-2309-13801.creator: Maria J. D. Lima, Flávio L. C. de Moura
arxiv-2309-13801.description: Abstract The substitution lemma is a renowned theorem within the realm of λ \lambda -calculus theory and concerns the interactional behaviour of the metasubstitution operation. In this work, we augment the λ \lambda -calculus’s grammar with an uninterpreted explicit substitution operator, which allows the use of our framework for different calculi with explicit substitutions.

arxiv-2404-11540.title: Bremsstrahlung Radiation Power in Fusion Plasmas Revisited: Towards Accurate Analytical Fitting
arxiv-2404-11540.creator: Huasheng Xie
arxiv-2404-11540.description: Abstract In fusion plasmas, where electron temperatures T e T_{e} range from keV to hundreds of keV, Bremsstrahlung radiation constitutes a significant energy loss mechanism. While various thermal average fitting formulas exist in the literature, their accuracy is limited, particularly for T e ≤ 20 T_{e}\leq 20 keV with error > 10 % >10\% .

arxiv-2407-01634.title: Brownian thermal birefringent noise due to non-diagonal anisotropic photoelastic effect in multilayer coated mirrors
arxiv-2407-01634.creator: Yu-Pei Zhang, Shi-Xiang Yang, Wen-Hai Tan, Cheng-Gang Shao, Yiqiu Ma, Shan-Qing Yang
arxiv-2407-01634.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yu-Pei Zhang, Shi-Xiang Yang, Wen-Hai Tan, Cheng-Gang Shao, Yiqiu Ma, Shan-Qing Yang. Thermal noise in the mirror coatings limits the accuracy of today’s most optical precision measurement experiments. Unlike the more commonly discussed thermal phase noise, the crystalline coating can generate thermal birefringent noise due to its anisotropic nature. In this study, we propose that the non-diagonal anisotropic photoelastic effect induced by the Brownian motion of mirror coating layers may contribute to this noise.

arxiv-2409-12867.title: Complex solutions of polynomial equations on the unit circle Thanks: This work was supported by EPSRC Open Fellowship EP/X009823/1. For the purpose of open access, the author has applied a Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) licence to any Author Accepted Manuscript version arising from this submis
arxiv-2409-12867.creator: Vahagn Aslanyan
arxiv-2409-12867.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Vahagn Aslanyan. We explore systems of polynomial equations where we seek complex solutions with absolute value 1. Geometrically, this amounts to understanding intersections of algebraic varieties with tori – Cartesian powers of the unit circle. We study the properties of varieties in which this intersection is Zariski dense, give a criterion for Zariski density and use it to show that the problem is decidable.

arxiv-2503-07596.title: Denoising Hamiltonian Network for Physical Reasoning
arxiv-2503-07596.creator: Congyue Deng, Brandon Y. Feng, Cecilia Garraffo, Alan Garbarz, Robin Walters, William T. Freeman, Leonidas Guibas, Kaiming He
arxiv-2503-07596.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Congyue Deng, Brandon Y. Feng, Cecilia Garraffo, Alan Garbarz, Robin Walters, William T. Freeman, Leonidas Guibas, Kaiming He. Machine learning frameworks for physical problems must capture and enforce physical constraints that preserve the structure of dynamical systems. Many existing approaches achieve this by integrating physical operators into neural networks.

arxiv-2505-13793.title: Statistical Properties of Predicted Blended Eclipsing Binary False Positives in PLATO LOPS 2024 Statistical Properties of Predicted Blended Eclipsing Binary False Positives in PLATO LOPS – References
arxiv-2505-13793.creator: J. C. Bray, U. Kolb, S. A. Mills
arxiv-2505-13793.description: Abstract With the planned launch of the PLAnetary Transit and Oscillation of stars (PLATO) satellite mission in 2026, an understanding of the stellar properties and spatial distribution of astrophysical false positives (FPs) is essential to ensure the limited ground-based spectroscopy resources are used efficiently to target the most likely genuine planetary transit (PT) candidates.

arxiv-2507-12947.title: Circular-beam approximation for quantum channels in the turbulent atmosphere
arxiv-2507-12947.creator: I. Pechonkin, M. Klen, A. A. Semenov
arxiv-2507-12947.description: Abstract The evolution of quantum states of light in free-space channels is strongly influenced by atmospheric turbulence, posing a significant challenge for quantum communication. The transmittance in such channels randomly fluctuates. This effect is commonly described by the probability distribution of transmittance (PDT).

arxiv-2602-18756.title: Multiunit I.I.D. Prophet Inequalities via Extreme Value Asymptotics
arxiv-2602-18756.creator: Jieming Kong Karthyek Murthy
arxiv-2602-18756.description: Abstract . We study the i.i.d. k k -selection prophet inequality problem, where a decision-maker sequentially observes n n independent nonnegative rewards and may accept at most k k of them without knowledge of future realizations. The objective is to maximize the expected total reward relative to that of a prophet who observes all rewards in advance.

arxiv-2602-24258.title: A model of tuberculosis progression using CompuCell3D
arxiv-2602-24258.creator: James W. G. Doran, Christopher F. Rowlatt, Gibin G. Powathil, Ruth Bowness, Christian A. Yates
arxiv-2602-24258.description: Abstract Tuberculosis (TB) is an airborne disease caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( M. tb ). Prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, TB was the leading cause of death from an infectious agent globally. However, most people exposed to M. tb do not develop active TB and go on to display symptoms.

arxiv-2604-07624.creator: Achintya Desai, Md Shafiuzzaman, Wenbo Guo, Tevfik Bultan

plos-pone-0002742.creator: Volker Huge, Meike Lauchart, Stefanie Förderreuther et al.
plos-pone-0002742.description: PLOS ONE research article. Sensory abnormalities are a key feature of Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS). In order to characterise these changes in patients suffering from acute or chronic CRPS I, we used Quantitative Sensory Testing (QST) in comparison to an age and gender matched control group. 61 pat

pmc-11453482.title: 8267 A Case of Pineal Gland Cyst and Adrenal Adenoma- Is this a New Syndrome?
pmc-11453482.creator: Mahrukh SIDDIQUI, Ummara Rafat, Shayann Shaik, Janice L Gilden
pmc-11453482.description: Disclosure: M. Siddiqui: None. U. Rafat: None. S. Shaik: None. J.L. Gilden: None. Background: The Pineal Gland receives information through a complex multi-neuronal pathway and is responsible for the secretion of melatonin, a hormone regulated by circadian rhythm and suppressed by light stimuli.

pmc-11532497.title: Investigation of linear and microscopic nonlinear optical responses of 1-indanone compounds in different environments based on polarity models
pmc-11532497.creator: Mahsa Khadem Sadigh, Z Sayyar, A N Shamkhali, R Teimuri-Mofrad, K Rahimpour
pmc-11532497.description: Molecular spectroscopic and nonlinear features can indicate positive changes by solvent molecules. In this work, DFT and spectroscopic techniques were used to study the polarity effects of different solvent environments. Polarity-based models were used for studying solvent induced interactions on the optical features of new groups of biomolecules.

pmc-12373778.title: Radiomics early assessment of post chemotherapy cardiotoxicity in cancer patients using 2D echocardiography imaging an interpretable machine learning study
pmc-12373778.creator: Masumeh Ahmadi, Erfan Barzegar-Golmoghani, Amir Ghaffari Jolfayi, Mobin Mohebi, Azin Alizadehasl, Mina Mohseni, Ahmad Bitarafan-Rajabi
pmc-12373778.description: Cardiotoxicity is the loss of the heart muscle’s ability to contract effectively, often due to chemotherapy or radiation therapy. This study uses interpretable machine learning to predict post-chemotherapy cardiotoxicity using radiomics features extracted from the baseline echocardiography images. The study involved 100 cancer patients at Rajaei Cardiovascular Medical and Research Center.

pmc-13010922.title: Volatilomics analysis reveals marker compounds for assessing chicken freshness and detecting frozen-thawed Korean native chicken
pmc-13010922.creator: Zubayed Ahamed, Jeong-Uk Eom, Han-Sul Yang
pmc-13010922.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study investigated the impact of frozen storage on the volatile compound profile of Korean native chicken (KNC) breast and identified marker compounds for freshness assessment and detection of frozen–thawed meat. Fresh samples were analyzed 2 hours postmortem, while frozen-thawed samples were stored at -18 °C for 7 days, thawed at 4 °C for 16 hours, and analyzed for volatiles using HS-SPME-GC-MS. The analysis identified 38 volatile compounds, with aldehydes, being the most prevalent.

pmc-13051055.title: Metastasis-Associated Wound Repair Promotes Reciprocal Lung Epithelium Activation and Breast Cancer Metastatic Outgrowth
pmc-13051055.creator: Jessica L. Christenson, Nicole S. Spoelstra, Michelle M. Williams, Linda L. Logan, Kathleen I. O’Neill, David J. Orlicky, Nolan T. Baker, Jennifer A. Wagner, Alyse W. Staley, Adrie Van Bokhoven, Andrew Goodspeed, Li-Wei Kuo, Lyndsey S. Crump, Jennifer R. Diamond, Jennifer K. Richer
pmc-13051055.description: When tumor cells colonize distant organs during metastasis, they interact extensively with surrounding cells. These interactions often change the behavior of surrounding cell populations which collectively induce a protumor microenvironment that permits tumor cell outgrowth into overt, clinically detectable metastatic disease. The lung is one of the most common sites of breast cancer metastasis.

pmc-13072706.title: Strengthening pharmacovigilance through patient reporting: a scoping review of awareness, barriers, and facilitators
pmc-13072706.creator: Adeel Aslam, Hafizah Abdul Majid, Nimra Muhammad Boota, Asma Ghulam Mustafa, Sumera Saeed Akhtar
pmc-13072706.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAdverse drug reactions (ADRs) significantly impact global healthcare systems, yet patient participation in pharmacovigilance remains underutilised. This scoping review synthesises evidence on patient awareness, barriers, and facilitators for ADR reporting to inform strategies for enhancing pharmacovigilance systems.MethodsFollowing the Arksey and O’Malley framework, we conducted a scoping review of studies published up to 2025 across PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar.

pmc-13195874.title: Epithelial CD155–TIGIT/CD226 signaling links CD8⁺ T-cell exhaustion to frequent exacerbations in COPD
pmc-13195874.creator: Dan Wang, Hui Li, Zhijun Zhao, Jiale Zhao, Xiaolan Hai, Yuchun Fan, Weirong Ma, Juan Chen, Xiahui Ge, Xiangguo Duan, Jia Hou
pmc-13195874.description: BackgroundThe immune mechanisms underlying chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain incompletely understood, particularly regarding immune checkpoint dysregulation. This cross-sectional observational study aimed to determine whether activation of the T-cell immunoglobulin and ITIM domain (TIGIT) pathway contributes to CD8-positive T-cell exhaustion and susceptibility to frequent exacerbations in COPD.

pmc-13373205.title: Acute ischemic stroke, active malignancy and non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis: an exploratory prospective observational study
pmc-13373205.creator: Athanasios Frydas, Ela Marie Akay, Hong Ran, Kudrat Rakhimov, Sarah Ouldali, Mazen Merhi, Frieder Pfäfflin, Linda Jürgens, Wolfram Doehner, Frank Tacke, Dominik Paul Modest, Anne Flörcken, Ingo Hilgendorf, Daniel Armando Morris, Eberhard Siebert, Christoph Leithner, Maximilian Schoels, Matthias Schn
pmc-13373205.description: About 3–10% of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) have active cancer. Malignancy-associated hypercoagulability (MAH) is an established cause of cancer-associated stroke. Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) is a severe manifestation of MAH. However, no prospective study has examined its prevalence and anticoagulation management in AIS.

pmc-13480053.title: Clinical presentation domains and venous anatomical patterns in cerebral venous thrombosis: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13480053.creator: Amirreza Radfar, Etrat Hooshmandi, Vahid Reza Ostovan, Sedighe Hooshmandi, Maryam Poursadeghfard, Nima Fadakar, Mahnaz Bayat
pmc-13480053.description: BackgroundCerebral venous thrombosis (CVT) presents with heterogeneous clinical manifestations that may partly reflect differences in venous anatomical involvement. However, systematic evaluation of structured clinical presentation domains in relation to distinct venous involvement patterns remains limited.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of consecutive adult patients with radiologically confirmed CVT at a tertiary referral center between 2017 and 2025.

pmc-13589992.title: Concurrent RUNX1::MECOM and RUNX1::PRDM16 Fusions from a Novel Genomic Breakpoint: First Report of a Dual-Fusion Mechanism in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
pmc-13589992.creator: Siyu Chen, Shengwang Wu, Jing Zhang, Xing Qiang, Siheng Liu, Wuchen Yang, Xiangui Peng, Xi Zhang, Jun Ren, Cheng Zhang
pmc-13589992.description: While complex fusions involving three chromosomes are already uncommon in AML, the formation of two distinct fusion genes from an identical breakpoint is exceptionally rare. This paper reports the adult case of acute myeloid leukemia harboring dual fusion genes RUNX1::MECOM and RUNX1::PRDM16, both originating from the same RUNX1 breakpoint (chr21:36206707, hg19).

pmc-13653019.title: An inducible co-stimulator ligand (ICOSL)-based peptide therapy for proteinuric kidney diseases targeting αvβ3 integrin
pmc-13653019.creator: Alexis P Jimenez-Uribe, Yan Xu, Yanxia Cao, Ryan Spear, Kwi Hye Koh, Adrian P Mansini, Ariana G Alcantar, Felix Kliewe, Nicole Endlich, Jochen Reiser, Steve Mangos, Eunsil Hahm
pmc-13653019.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Dysregulated αvβ3 integrin activation in podocytes contributes to proteinuric kidney disease by disrupting podocyte architecture and the glomerular filtration barrier. However, no treatments currently exist that therapeutically target this integrin. We previously identified inducible co-stimulator ligand (ICOSL) as an endogenous antagonist of αvβ3 integrin that protects kidney function through its arginine-glycine-aspartic acid (RGD) motif, independent of its canonical role in immunity.
